title: R-20 and R-22 ruled and implemented: a registration binds its principal and is never overwritten, and the four connector authority routes refuse an unresolved caller identically
rulings_carried: R-20 (owner-ruled, implemented as a HOLDER CHECK, not a principal in the id): register resolves its caller first, records owner_ref (server-resolved), and refuses an existing id 409 connector_already_registered for every caller, the holder included; pre-ruling records are never backfilled and never re-keyed. Why not principal-in-id: re-keying would orphan every record that names connector:<id> (session profiles are closed sets; lease grants, standing leases and credentials join on the id), and the ruling forbids a silent re-key.

R-22 (owner-ruled): register, bind, revoke and invoke answer an unresolved caller 401 hypervisor.authentication_required, byte-identical, before any record read; invoke's local-operator literal and its unreachable principal_required arm are gone; the act tool inherits the refusal.

Posture: auth_gate defaults to auto (enforce only when exposed or forwarded); the served App stamps x-ioi-forwarded only for a non-loopback browser; bootstrap sets no policy. The shipped alpha enables enforcement NOWHERE, so in-handler resolution is the entire gate; every verifier boots its daemon the same way.
